key_insight: Biology-guided transcriptomic features outperformed unstable gene-by-gene selection and added the most predictive value for immunotherapy response in advanced urothelial carcinoma.
clinical_relevance: For patients already assessed with standard clinical and biomarker data, pathway-informed transcriptomic profiling may better identify likely responders to atezolizumab than ad hoc gene selection.
method: 298 IMvigor210 patients with advanced urothelial carcinoma were analyzed.
Compared knowledge-guided tumor microenvironment gene sets versus data-driven transcriptome-wide gene selection.
Tested incremental AUPRC gains over clinical variables, standard biomarkers, and expanded biomarker sets.
evidence_signal: Knowledge-guided features improved AUPRC by 0.058 over clinical variables alone and by 0.011 to 0.016 beyond biomarker-rich baselines, while external evaluation showed a similar advantage pattern.
watch_item: The data-driven gene selection was unstable across folds, so findings may not translate cleanly without robust external validation and standardized feature representation.
paper_title: Incremental Predictive Value and Representation of Transcriptomic Features for Immunotherapy Response in Advanced Urothelial Carcinoma
